issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The change trains 5 LightGBM models on the descriptor features with seeds seed..seed+4 and averages their predictions. It uses only the training labels, reads no files and touches no test labels.

No bugs. desc_features is now computed once and reused, the 5 predictions are averaged correctly (each divided by 5), and every seed comes from the seed argument. LightGBM runtime goes up by about 5x, which should still fit easily within the 10-minute limit.
Recomputed z with noise sd 0.0070: the difference is 0.4968 - 0.4932 = 0.0036, the standard error is 0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ 0.42. This matches the harness value of 0.422.

The decision is consistent with the numbers. A gain of 0.0036 from a single run is well inside the noise, so rejecting it provisionally (or running a replicate) is justified. Averaging over seeds only reduces the variance of the LightGBM part, so any real gain is probably small.
